entry.title: Site: RFC 0003 opened for comment, with a window of 23 November 2026 to 8 January 2027 and an issue as the comment ...
entry.content:
23 November 2026.

RFC 0003 opened for comment, with a window of 23 November 2026 to 8 January 2027 and an issue as the comment thread: RFC 0003, a profile defining the five workforce health measures the UK government has named and not defined (work ability, absence, sustained return, retention and disability participation), a minimum group size rule that names the floors already in the specification and sets out how small numbers are withheld or merged, and two proposed record types, CommitmentEvent for the dated commitments and ProviderReturn for a common group-level return from a provider to an employer. The three proposals can be decided separately. Nothing in the specification changes until a decision is recorded, and none of it is endorsed by any government department, by BSI or by anyone else. The open review page lists it, and now says that the comment windows for RFCs 0001 and 0002 closed on 17 October 2026 with no decision yet recorded.

entry.title: Site: A new page, Check a file, checks one v0.2 record or an entity-graph bundle in the browser and explains each ...
entry.content:
19 November 2026.

A new page, Check a file, checks one v0.2 record or an entity-graph bundle in the browser and explains each failure: the field, the rule and what the specification says. It runs the repository's own tools/validate.py and tools/check_entity_graph.py, unchanged, in Python compiled to WebAssembly, so its verdicts are the reference validator's; a test runs all 147 example files through both and fails on any difference. The file is not uploaded or sent anywhere: the page fetches only its own files from this site, makes no request while it checks, and has no visit counter. The footer of every page and the home page's door for software builders link to it, and the privacy page says it contacts no outside service. A pass means structurally conformant at Level 1. The page says that Level 2 and Level 3 are not checked.

entry.title: Site: The pages that name the specification version say v0.2 draft: the home page, Inside the standard, How it ...
entry.content:

The entity map is described as drawn for v0.1 and unchanged in v0.2, since v0.2 adds no entity and removes none, and its two reserved names read "no fields yet" rather than "no fields in v0.1"; both labellings are generated from the drawing's source, and a check refuses a page whose spliced drawing differs from fresh generation. Corrected: the entity-map legends, How it works and the standard page said individual records are never employer-visible and the aggregate report is the only output that leaves, which contradicted the specification's expressly classified individual-employer fields; they now say that aggregate-only values reach an employer through a report satisfying the privacy profile, that individual instrument results are never employer-visible, and that only the expressly classified individual-employer fields may be disclosed at individual grain under the independent-legal-basis condition. The v0.1 release archive is served byte for byte as published, and a check refuses a substitute. The current v0.2 download and the site's copies of the schemas, examples and code lists are checked against the repository sources on every change, and a stale download is refused. The README names both drafts.
